title: Breach Breakdown: How One Cyberattack Stalled Boston Scientific's Factories and Shipping
description:
On August 25, 2026, medical device maker Boston Scientific found unauthorized activity on its systems. A network outage cut access to some operating systems and business applications, and for a while the company could not manufacture, process or ship some customer orders. Here is the timeline, what it cost, what is still unknown, and four lessons for any business.

Timeline
- August 25: incident identified; network outage.
- August 26: first disclosure in an SEC filing (Form 8-K).
- September 8: second 8-K says the company is unlikely to meet its Q3 and full-year 2026 sales growth and adjusted EPS guidance.
- October 28: Q3 2026 results.

What it cost
- Manufacturing and shipments were disrupted for eight business days, according to reports of the earnings call.
- Q3 2026 net sales: $5.138 billion, up 1.5%, below a 3% to 5% outlook. Management estimated the incident cut about 3 percentage points of growth (as reported from the earnings call).
- Q4 2026 net sales now expected to fall 1% to 3%. Full-year 2026 reported growth about 4.25%, down from 5.5% to 6.5% guided in July.

Still unknown
So far, Boston Scientific has not disclosed how the attackers got in. No group has publicly claimed the attack, and ransomware or data theft have not been confirmed.

Four lessons for any business (Securidge analysis)
1. List what must keep running if IT goes dark.
2. Rehearse a manual way to take and ship orders.
3. Keep offline backups, and test restoring them.
4. Separate factory systems from office IT.
